stories.title: Government to function normally while Burnham on holiday, No 10 says
stories.summary: Andy Burnham is taking a break with his family after entering No 10 two weeks ago. His spokesman confirmed he remains in contact with officials and will continue holding meetings while away, amid criticism from Kemi Badenoch that he had 'bunked off'.

stories.title: Burnham to embark on cost-of-living tour through the UK
stories.summary: The Prime Minister is set to tour the UK's nations and regions in 'listening mode', working on what Downing Street calls a '10-year plan to bring back hope'. Burnham wrote in the Guardian that he will tackle consumer 'rip-offs' including subscriptions that can't easily be cancelled.

stories.title: Burnham launches 'national drive' to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
stories.summary: The Prime Minister has announced a national initiative to end rough sleeping by Christmas, backed by the £340m already committed to rough sleeping support during his first week in office.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 DSIT scrapped: AI minister role boosted but technology department axed in Burnham shake-up
stories.summary: PM Burnham abolished the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), moving AI and science policy into a new Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and digital/online safety into a renamed DCMS. Tech advocates have expressed alarm at the potential loss of dedicated tech governance focus.

stories.title: 🤖 GDS updates legacy IT definition to focus on 'risk rather than age'
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service has revised how it categorises legacy IT systems, shifting the focus from the age of technology to the risk it poses — a signal of a more nuanced, outcome-driven approach to public sector digital transformation.

stories.title: 🤖 Home Office targets AI-generated savings with police non-emergency phone line
stories.summary: The Home Office is piloting AI to handle police non-emergency (101) calls, aiming to generate efficiency savings. The initiative reflects the Burnham government's whole-of-government AI adoption push following the abolition of DSIT.

stories.title: 🏗️ DWP plans £1bn programme to consolidate use of digital freelancers
stories.summary: The Department for Work and Pensions is planning a major £1bn programme to rationalise and consolidate its use of digital contractors and freelancers — a significant procurement signal for the contingent labour market in government.

stories.title: 🤝 Andy Burnham tells Labour MPs he will rein in Britain's outsourcing industry
stories.summary: PM Burnham has signalled to Labour MPs that he intends to significantly curtail the government's use of private outsourcing, with £400bn of public money currently spent on government contracts annually. This is a major signal for consulting and service delivery firms.

stories.title: 💰 Can Andy Burnham rewire the 'Treasury brain' to boost growth?
stories.summary: Analysis of whether Burnham can shift Treasury orthodoxy to unlock greater public investment and local growth, as he battles established fiscal constraints inherited from the Starmer era. Key test for his economic agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 Why trust is the foundation of data-driven government — Government Chief Data Officer
stories.summary: The Government Chief Data Officer, Aimee Smith, has published a piece on the three foundational principles for data-driven public services — with trust highlighted as the critical third pillar alongside data quality and sharing.

stories.title: 🏢 Newcastle City Council deploys AWS AI tools to improve customer support
stories.summary: Newcastle City Council has implemented Amazon Web Services AI tools to improve citizen-facing customer support — a vendor signal reflecting continued AWS expansion in local public sector despite national debates over US tech dependencies.

stories.title: 🚦 Sentencing Act early release scheme paused by Burnham
stories.summary: PM Burnham paused the Sentencing Act early release scheme — which was due to come into force on 2 September — following criticism from survivors, victims' families and opposition politicians. This reversal of a Starmer-era programme signals Burnham's intent to distance himself on law and order.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, House of Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Parliament in summer recess — returns in September
stories.summary: The House of Commons and House of Lords are in summer recess. Parliament is scheduled to return in September, when opposition parties have promised to intensify scrutiny of Burnham's first months in office.

topics.name: Labour Party
topics.description: Labour Party news, policy, internal politics

stories.title: Scottish Labour leadership contest: Michael Marra and Joe Fagan on ballot
stories.summary: The Scottish Labour leadership race is now down to two candidates — Michael Marra MSP and Joe Fagan — after Monica Lennon failed to secure enough nominations. Marra has placed himself on the 'soft left' and co-wrote Scottish Labour's 2026 manifesto; Fagan is seen as a more centrist candidate.

stories.title: Lennon criticises 'nasty' Scottish Labour as leadership bid fails
stories.summary: MSP Monica Lennon, a trans rights supporter, failed to secure enough nominations for the Scottish Labour leadership race and criticised the party's direction on LGBTQ issues. The contest was triggered when Anas Sarwar stepped down to join Andy Burnham's UK government.

stories.title: Labour delivering on 'Plan for Change' as Burnham sets priorities
stories.summary: The Labour Party website is now promoting Burnham's Plan for Change as the governing agenda, having updated its platform following the leadership transition. Early priorities include cost-of-living measures, rough sleeping, and social care reform.

stories.title: Badenoch says Reform defectors 'some of the most dishonest people I have met'
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch launched a sharp attack on former Tory MPs who defected to Reform UK, calling them deeply dishonest. The comments came amid ongoing tensions as Badenoch seeks to consolidate her right-flank leadership strategy.

stories.title: Badenoch's 'weird week': defence of ex-neo-Nazi candidate raises questions
stories.summary: Badenoch faced intense scrutiny after a former neo-Nazi activist was selected as a Conservative council candidate in Somerset. She also announced plans to evict foreign nationals with leave to remain from social housing, drawing criticism from charities and Reform UK alike.

stories.title: Badenoch pledges to exclude pro-ECHR and pro-net zero candidates from standing as Conservatives
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch has written that centrist or 'one nation' Tories who support ECHR membership or net zero targets will be blocked as candidates in the next election. The move has alarmed some in the party and European counterparts.

stories.title: Lib Dems positioning as alternative to Reform and Greens extremes, says Davey
stories.summary: Ed Davey has sought to position the Liberal Democrats as the moderate, reasonable choice against what he characterises as the extremes of Reform UK on the right and the Greens on the left. The party is building out its electoral operation ahead of the next general election.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Reform UK, Nigel Farage news and announcements

stories.title: Farage wins Clacton by-election but parliamentary investigation resumes immediately
stories.summary: Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election with 22,239 votes against Count Binface in second place (9,455), as major parties boycotted the contest. Within hours, the parliamentary standards watchdog resumed its investigation into the £5m undeclared gift from billionaire Christopher Harborne.

stories.title: Standards watchdog resumes Farage probe as rivals slam 'needless byelection'
stories.summary: The parliamentary standards commissioner has resumed its formal investigation into Farage's failure to register the £5m gift. Two separate standards investigations are due to conclude in autumn — one on the Harborne gift, another on benefits received from convicted fraudster George Cottrell.

stories.title: The tangled financial web at the heart of Reform UK
stories.summary: An in-depth investigation has detailed how Reform UK has been funded: including a secret £5m gift, behind-the-scenes loans from donors, and a Metropolitan Police investigation in which two people were interviewed under caution. Financial industry sources say transactions have been referred to the National Crime Agency.

stories.title: Scottish Labour leadership contest linked to Sarwar's departure to Burnham government
stories.summary: The SNP faces a changed Scottish political landscape as Anas Sarwar has left to join the Burnham government, triggering a Scottish Labour leadership contest. The SNP, which took the most Holyrood seats but missed a majority in 2026, faces renewed opposition from a potentially reinvigorated Labour in Scotland.

stories.title: Scottish Parliament rejects call for Peter Murrell inquiry
stories.summary: The Scottish Parliament has voted against a formal inquiry into the crimes of former SNP chief executive Peter Murrell, instead backing a different oversight approach. The Murrell embezzlement scandal continues to cast a shadow over the SNP's reputation.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Burnham's full cabinet confirmed: Louise Haigh as First Secretary and CDL
stories.summary: The Burnham cabinet is confirmed with Louise Haigh as First Secretary of State and Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster (Minister for the Cabinet Office), John Healey as Chancellor, and Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary. Matthew Pennycook continues as housing minister, now attending cabinet.

stories.title: No 10 North established as Manchester base for PM operations
stories.summary: As part of his first week in office, Burnham formally established 'No 10 North' — a Manchester-based operation intended as the 'nerve centre of a rewired Britain'. The Cabinet Office is providing the institutional infrastructure, drawing together devolution, investment, and public services reform teams.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Farage wins Clacton by-election: Reform UK leader returned with 22,239 votes
stories.summary: Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election he triggered by resigning his seat. Major parties (Labour, Conservative, Lib Dems) boycotted the contest. Count Binface came second with 9,455 votes. The win is symbolic but parliamentary and police investigations into Farage's finances continue.

stories.title: 2026 local elections: Reform biggest winner with 1,451 new seats; Labour loses 1,493 councillors
stories.summary: Reform UK emerged as the biggest winner in England's 2026 local elections, gaining 1,451 council seats. Labour lost 1,493 councillors. The Liberal Democrats gained 155 seats while Conservatives lost 563. The Greens gained 438 new seats.

stories.title: No major House of Lords news in the 48-hour window
stories.summary: The House of Lords is in summer recess. No significant Lords debates, appointments, or reform announcements were reported in the Fri-Mon window. The Lords is expected to return in September alongside the Commons.
